FileBoardSource.check_drift()/resolve() resolve a REF.PAD against the current board and compare the recorded net name, raising named PadNotFoundError (broken identity), AmbiguousPadError (cross-net collision), or NetDriftError (net renamed). TestDriftDiagnostics and test_rerouted_board_same_ref_pad_still_resolves_geometry in tests/test_board_source.py demonstrate 'a rerouted board resolves the same paths or produces a named drift error' at the BoardSource layer. A REF.PAD name that collides across different nets (e.g. a multi-pad component whose pads all share one generic pin function) does not fail FileBoardSource construction; it fails only pad()/check_drift()/resolve() calls that name it specifically, with AmbiguousPadError. Confirmed against real data: the IP5385 reference board's LED1 footprint has this collision.

Cross-net REF.PAD collisions are rejected with AmbiguousPadError, but lazily (on lookup of that specific name) rather than at FileBoardSource construction: a name can only recur across _build_pad_index's per-net groups as a genuine cross-net collision (same-net duplicates are already collapsed by _terminals_for_net first), but raising eagerly would make the IP5385 reference board's one ambiguous LED1 component brick lookup of every other terminal on an otherwise 200-footprint board

Pads sharing one REF.PAD name are collapsed only when they also share one net; cross-net collisions raise AmbiguousPadError instead (revised in this response after review)

known_issues: The IP5385 reference board contains a genuine REF.PAD ambiguity: LED1's five pads all share pin function "1" while sitting on five different nets (76, 77, 78, 79, 113), so LED1.1 cannot resolve to one terminal. This is a characteristic of that board's own data, not a code defect, and is exactly the case AmbiguousPadError exists to report. Because ref_pad_name() always prefers a truthy pin function over the bare pad name, LED1's individual pads are not addressable via pad("LED1.<n>") at all; a future session needing one of them individually should use pads(net=...) or terminals(net, dedupe=False) instead.
